From fbb77611e95d3d5b2af86a59754a3130877cb667 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Dmitry V. Levin" <ldv@altlinux.org>
Date: Sat, 5 Aug 2017 23:00:50 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] Fix compat_sys_sigpending breakage

The latest change of compat_sys_sigpending in commit 8f13621abced
("sigpending(): move compat to native") has broken it in two ways.

First, it tries to write 4 bytes more than userspace expects:
sizeof(old_sigset_t) == sizeof(long) == 8 instead of
sizeof(compat_old_sigset_t) == sizeof(u32) == 4.

Second, on big endian architectures these bytes are being written in the
wrong order.

This bug was found by strace test suite.

Reported-by: Anatoly Pugachev <matorola@gmail.com>
Inspired-by: Eugene Syromyatnikov <evgsyr@gmail.com>
Fixes: 8f13621abced ("sigpending(): move compat to native")
Signed-off-by: Dmitry V. Levin <ldv@altlinux.org>
Acked-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

diff --git a/kernel/signal.c b/kernel/signal.c
index caed9133ae52..7e33f8c583e6 100644
--- a/kernel/signal.c
+++ b/kernel/signal.c
@@ -3303,12 +3303,15 @@ SYSCALL_DEFINE1(sigpending, old_sigset_t __user *, set)
 #ifdef CONFIG_COMPAT
 COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE1(sigpending, compat_old_sigset_t __user *, set32)
 {
+#ifdef __BIG_ENDIAN
 	sigset_t set;
-	int err = do_sigpending(&set, sizeof(old_sigset_t)); 
-	if (err == 0)
-		if (copy_to_user(set32, &set, sizeof(old_sigset_t)))
-			err = -EFAULT;
+	int err = do_sigpending(&set, sizeof(set.sig[0]));
+	if (!err)
+		err = put_user(set.sig[0], set32);
 	return err;
+#else
+	return sys_rt_sigpending((sigset_t __user *)set32, sizeof(*set32));
+#endif
 }
 #endif
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `kernel/signal.c`**
   - The `sigpending` function for compatibility (`COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE1(sigpending, compat_old_sigset_t __user *, set32)`) has been modified to address two main issues:
     - The size of the signal set being handled has been corrected. Instead of using `sizeof(old_sigset_t)`, which is 8 bytes, it now uses `sizeof(set.sig[0])`, which is appropriate for the size of the signal set on the architecture.
     - The handling of the signal set for big-endian architectures has been adjusted. A conditional compilation directive (`#ifdef __BIG_ENDIAN`) has been added to ensure that the correct byte order is used when writing the signal set to user space. If the architecture is big-endian, it uses `put_user` to write the first element of the signal set directly to `set32`. If not, it calls `sys_rt_sigpending` with a cast to handle the signal set.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modifications in `kernel/signal.c` are directly related to the bug introduced in the previous commit (8f13621abced) that moved the compatibility implementation of `sigpending` to a native implementation. The patch addresses the two specific issues that arose from that change: incorrect size handling and byte order for big-endian architectures. By correcting these issues, the patch ensures that the `sigpending` function behaves as expected in both compatibility and native contexts, thus restoring the intended functionality that was broken by the earlier commit.

Here is the commit message:
Fix compat_sys_sigpending breakage

The latest change of compat_sys_sigpending in commit 8f13621abced
("sigpending(): move compat to native") has broken it in two ways.

First, it tries to write 4 bytes more than userspace expects:
sizeof(old_sigset_t) == sizeof(long) == 8 instead of
sizeof(compat_old_sigset_t) == sizeof(u32) == 4.

Second, on big endian architectures these bytes are being written in the
wrong order.

This bug was found by strace test suite.

Reported-by: Anatoly Pugachev <matorola@gmail.com>
Inspired-by: Eugene Syromyatnikov <evgsyr@gmail.com>
Fixes: 8f13621abced ("sigpending(): move compat to native")
Signed-off-by: Dmitry V. Levin <ldv@altlinux.org>
Acked-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
Signed-off-by: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `compat_sys_sigpending` function attempting to write a signal set of 8 bytes (the size of `old_sigset_t`) instead of the expected 4 bytes (the size of `compat_old_sigset_t`). Additionally, on big-endian architectures, the bytes were being written in the wrong order, leading to incorrect data being passed to user space.

Here is the patch:
 COMPAT_SYSCALL_DEFINE1(sigpending, compat_old_sigset_t __user *, set32)
 {
+#ifdef __BIG_ENDIAN
 	sigset_t set;
-	int err = do_sigpending(&set, sizeof(old_sigset_t)); 
-	if (err == 0)
-		if (copy_to_user(set32, &set, sizeof(old_sigset_t)))
-			err = -EFAULT;
+	int err = do_sigpending(&set, sizeof(set.sig[0]));
+	if (!err)
+		err = put_user(set.sig[0], set32);
 	return err;
+#else
+	return sys_rt_sigpending((sigset_t __user *)set32, sizeof(*set32));
+#endif
 }
 #endif
